name: Person

fields.label: Series
fields.description: Identifier series. 'PER-.####' numbers continuously; 'PER-.YY.-.####' restarts each year — the native equivalent of the original `sequence.reset_policy = yearly`.

fields.label: Display name
fields.description: Computed on save: English name, else Arabic name. Frappe's `title_field`, so link fields, list views and the global search show one readable name for a bilingual record.

fields.label: Name (original language)
fields.description: The name in the script and language of the source.

fields.label: Original-name language
fields.description: Native `Language` doctype — not a free-text language code.

fields.label: Transliteration
fields.description: Latin transliteration of the original-script name.

fields.label: Other recorded forms of the name
fields.description: Spellings met in sources that are not the preferred form. Searchable, so 'Mosul' finds 'Mūṣil'.

fields.label: Portrait
fields.description: Uploaded portrait (native File, permission-checked by Frappe).

fields.label: Portrait URL (external)
fields.description: Use for a portrait hosted elsewhere; the uploaded portrait wins when both are set.

fields.label: Portrait alt text
fields.description: Short description of the portrait for accessibility and print.

fields.label: Date of birth (as stated)
fields.description: A birth year alone is a legitimate value: '1912', 'c. 1912', '1910s'.

fields.label: Date of birth (comparable)
fields.description: Machine-comparable value derived from the 'as stated' value; used for filters, sorting and reports. Never more precise than what is stated.

fields.label: Date of birth precision
fields.options:
exact
minute
day
month
year
decade
approximate
uncertain
range
unknown
fields.description: How much of the date is actually known. 'approximate' keeps c. 1850; 'year' keeps 1850; 'decade' keeps '1850s'; 'minute' keeps a time of day.

fields.label: Date of death (as stated)
fields.description: Exactly as the source gives it: 1950 · 1950-05 · 1950-05-12 · 1950-05-12T21:45 · 'c. 1850' · '1850s' · '1850?'. Authoritative value; the date field beside it is derived from it.

fields.label: Date of death (comparable)
fields.description: Machine-comparable value derived from the 'as stated' value; used for filters, sorting and reports. Never more precise than what is stated.

fields.label: Date of death precision
fields.options:
exact
minute
day
month
year
decade
approximate
uncertain
range
unknown
fields.description: How much of the date is actually known. 'approximate' keeps c. 1850; 'year' keeps 1850; 'decade' keeps '1850s'; 'minute' keeps a time of day.

fields.label: Nationality
fields.description: Native `Country` master (ISO 3166). Remembers the last value picked: a recorder entering people from one country picks it once.

fields.label: Place of birth
fields.description: Association only — it never assigns that place's coordinates to this person.

fields.label: Place of birth (as stated)
fields.description: What the source says, kept verbatim even when the place cannot be linked to a Place record. Mandatory while no Place is linked: an unlinked place must still be recorded.

fields.label: Current status
fields.description: Living, deceased, whereabouts unknown …

fields.label: Category
fields.description: Military / Civilian / Other. The category decides which attributes apply: a military person shows rank, branch, commission date, service status and military biography; a civilian shows the career fields. This is the 2026 update that folded the separate `commander` (Leader) table into Person (migration 020).

fields.label: Current position (as stated)
fields.description: Free text as the source gives it. The structured, dated post is a row in Positions below.

fields.label: Declared affiliation (as stated)
fields.description: An affiliation the person (or a source) asserts but that is not corroborated. Corroborated posts go in Positions with 'Verified' ticked.

fields.label: Military service
fields.description: Service attributes that apply to a person of the military category. The row of a source's `commander` table is this section plus a Person record.

fields.label: Rank
fields.description: The rank held. Free text on purpose: a historical rank (Ottoman, mandate-era, foreign) must not be forced into a modern list.

fields.label: Service branch
fields.description: Army, Navy, Air Force, Joint, Gendarmerie, Coast Guard — a governed vocabulary (migration 020 domain `military_branch`), extendable without a code change.

fields.label: Commission date
fields.description: When the person was commissioned. A year alone is acceptable, which is why this is a plain Date and not the three-field historical-date trio: military commission records are day-precise in this dataset.

fields.label: Service status
fields.description: Active → Reserve → Retired, and Retired is terminal (source `SERVICE_STATUS_TRANSITIONS`). The transition is enforced in the controller; see Del. 12 §4.

fields.label: Military biography
fields.description: Service history, commands and campaigns — the military record behind the rank.

fields.label: Leadership qualities
fields.description: Judgements about a leader, one row per quality, and each row must carry its basis (who assessed it, when, on what evidence). The source keeps these in a separate `commander_trait`/`person_trait` table; a judgement about a person is owned by that person, so it is a child table here.

fields.label: Specialisations
fields.description: Governed vocabulary (Table MultiSelect). Free keywords are added with Frappe's native tags instead.

fields.label: Latitude
fields.description: This record's own latitude, independent of any linked place.

fields.label: Longitude
fields.description: This record's own longitude, independent of any linked place.

fields.label: Map (point)
fields.description: Select a point on the map. It is mirrored into the latitude and longitude fields and resolves the administrative hierarchy.

fields.label: 0,0 is an actual point
fields.description: Tick only when latitude 0 and longitude 0 are a deliberate real location; otherwise the zero pair is treated as unset.

fields.label: Coordinate precision
fields.description: How close the point is to the true position.

fields.label: How the point was obtained
fields.options:
manual
map_pick
coordinate_entry
gazetteer
administrative
city_centroid
geocoder
historical_map
inherited
fields.description: A city centroid is not a street address; recording the method stops a centroid from being read as a verified location.

fields.label: Uncertainty radius (m)
fields.description: The radius the true position could lie within.

fields.label: Point source
fields.description: The map, survey or gazetteer the coordinates came from.

fields.label: Locality / place name
fields.description: Nearest named place (village/town); auto-filled by reverse-geocoding.

fields.label: Primary source
fields.description: The source the record rests on. Additional claims from other sources are recorded in the Evidence table, one claim per row.

fields.label: Authentication level
fields.description: How strongly the record's content is verified.

fields.label: Record status
fields.description: Editorial state, driven by the SIRAJ Review workflow (Draft → In Review → Verified → Published, plus Needs Update / Disputed / Archived / Rejected).

fields.label: Researcher's notes
fields.description: Internal working notes. At permission level 1, so visible to reviewers and administrators only; discussion belongs in the document's comment thread instead.

fields.label: Evidence
fields.description: One row per claim: which source says what, where in the source, whether it supports or contradicts, and who verified it. Not copied with the record: a claim is evidence about one specific record.

fields.label: External identifiers
fields.description: VIAF, Wikidata, ORCID, library catalogue or legacy numbers, kept out of the record's own identifier. Never copied: an authority identifier belongs to exactly one record.

fields.label: Completeness (%)
fields.description: Share of the record's critical fields that are filled in. Computed on save; used by the quality report and by the 'minimum completeness to publish' rule. Completeness, not truth.

description: Researchers, scholars, officials and other individuals.
